subject: [Icefall11B] Elevated 5xx / timeouts — customer comms and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-22 09:04:00 -0000
Subject: [Monitoring] spike: icefall11b 5xx/timeouts (starting 09:02 UTC)

Hey team,

Monitoring alerted at 09:02 UTC for elevated 5xx and client-side timeouts against model icefall11b-p7 across two availability zones (us-west1-a/b). Current error rate ~6% for generation requests; p95 latency up ~2.1x. I pulled recent logs and pasted short snippets in the attached icefall11b-503-log-snippets.txt — seeing a mix of 503 responses from the inference layer and KV-cache mismatch NACKs.

Immediate asks:
- Can infra confirm if any recent kernel/quantization rollout touched icefall11b in the last 48h?
- Can we enable the small-fallback route for affected customers (icefall11b-small) while triage runs?

I flagged INF-7891.

- Marissa
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-22 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Re: [Monitoring] spike: icefall11b 5xx/timeouts (starting 09:02 UTC)

Thanks Marissa — looking. Quick update: we rolled kernel-selector v2.0 yesterday evening as part of a perf patch (no config changes expected for icefall11b), but I see a small percentage of workers reporting kernel mismatch during runtime selection which can cause config fallback to an unsupported code path that returns 503s under KV cache pressure.

I'll coordinate a hotfix (pin selector to v1.9 for the legacy runtime) and enable the icefall11b-small fallback route for high-traffic tenants. Ben, Monica — do you want me to push the route change now or wait for your sign-off?

- Karthik
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@acmesoft.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-22 09:27:00 -0000
Subject: Icefall11B: brief customer notice — elevated errors and mitigation

Elena —

We’re reaching out to let you know we observed elevated 5xx errors and timeouts impacting some Icefall11B-powered requests starting ~09:02 UTC this morning. Our engineering team is actively triaging; initial cause appears related to a kernel selector rollout that led to an unsupported runtime path under certain KV cache conditions.

What we’ve done so far:
- Enabled a temporary fallback to icefall11b-small for high-traffic requests from AcmeSoft (should reduce error rate quickly)
- Pinned the kernel-selector to the prior stable version for the affected worker pool
- Restarted the affected worker instances to clear stale cache state

Current status: error rate has dropped meaningfully to ~0.7% as of 09:25 UTC; we continue to monitor.

Next steps: we’ll follow up with a full RCA and planned permanent fix (kernel-selector patch + improved pre-deploy checks) within 48 hours. We’ll also share any logs and a short customer-facing summary once we complete the postmortem.

We apologize for the disruption. If you see ongoing failures on your side, let me know the request IDs and I’ll escalate to the on-call SRE immediately.

— Ben
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Elena Park <elena@acmesoft.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-22 09:36:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Icefall11B: brief customer notice — elevated errors and mitigation

Thanks Ben — we saw elevated 5xxs on our side as well (production traffic to icefall11b). Appreciate the quick fallback; we’ve routed a few test requests since and the failure rate looks much better. Please include our procurement/security contact (support@acmesoft.com) on the postmortem.

Elena
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Elena Park <elena@acmesoft.com>, support@acmesoft.com
Date: 2027-08-22 10:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Icefall11B: brief customer notice — elevated errors and mitigation

Follow-up: pinned selector and fallback route applied at 09:40 UTC; rollbacks completed without additional stability issues. We also applied a targeted restart to the two affected worker shards to clear kernel caches. Post-change metrics: 5xx rate <0.5% across affected clusters; p95 latency returning to baseline.

I’ve attached a short runbook (runbook-icefall11b-patch-v1.pdf) describing the emergency mitigation steps and the patch we’ll validate for the permanent fix. Planning note: permanent fix will include a change to the kernel-selector to validate compatibility before switching and a preflight that simulates KV cache pressure.

- Karthik
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Elena Park <elena@acmesoft.com>, support@acmesoft.com
Date: 2027-08-23 15:12:00 -0000
Subject: Icefall11B — recovery confirmation and preliminary RCA

Elena and team —

Quick recovery confirmation: we completed the initial RCA and a targeted remediation yesterday (pinned selector + worker restart + fallback route). The service remained stable overnight and through today’s peak.

Preliminary RCA (summary):
- Trigger: kernel-selector v2.0 rollout selected an optimized kernel path for a subset of Icefall11B workers.
- Fault: under specific KV cache pressure patterns (short bursty sessions with many small prefixes), the optimized kernel attempted to access an uninitialized path causing an immediate 503 return from the runtime.
- Mitigation applied: rollback to selector v1.9 for legacy pools, enable icefall11b-small fallback, restart affected workers to clear bad kernel state.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Karthik: release selector v2.0.1 with compatibility checks and preflight simulation (ETA 2027-08-25 EOD)
- Marissa: extend monitoring to include KV cache mismatch alerts and a new synthetic that replicates bursty short-prefix traffic (ETA 2027-08-24 18:00 UTC)
- Monica / Customer Success: share final postmortem and a credit offer for impacted calls (Monica to coordinate Acme billing)

Attached is the customer notice we sent (customer-notice-acmesoft-20270822.pdf) and log snippets. We’ll send a finalized postmortem with timelines and remediation verification once the v2.0.1 patch passes staging.

Apologies again for the disruption — happy to jump on a call if you’d like a live walkthrough.

— Ben
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Elena Park <elena@acmesoft.com>, support@acmesoft.com
Date: 2027-08-23 15:28:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Icefall11B — recovery confirmation and preliminary RCA

Elena — we’ll follow up with the formal postmortem and a small usage credit for the calls that returned 5xx between 09:02–09:40 UTC on 2027-08-22. I’ll coordinate with Acme billing and include documentation of mitigations. Expect the formal postmortem by 2027-08-25.

Thanks for the quick verification earlier, and appreciate the patience.

— Monica
